context:
The analysis you asked for, from o2's lane, measured in claude-settings history: 155 commit messages cite 542 record paths. 471 of those files no longer exist anywhere, because sweeps deleted them; they did not move. The other 71 still exist, and o2's folder move breaks all 71 paths, while their ids still resolve.
Where a path cite has helped: (1) the 'Drops-lines' line in 82 commits, which the silent-undo check reads (the guard already exempts it); (2) an agent can open a live path at once, with no search; (3) banchi records cite docs/decisions/ paths in 5 files. The guard reads only commit messages and PR text, so those files are untouched.
What cite-by-id protects: a cite that still works after a move. o2's move is exactly that. Today the guard refuses only root decisions/ and debts/ paths, so after the move a docs/decisions/x.md cite passes, and the rule stops working here in practice.
home: PR #607 body, 'Questions parked for the owner', item 1

options.label: Leave the guard as it is
options.lose: The rule goes unenforced after the move, and the next move breaks every new cite.

options.gain: The rule holds through this move and any later one.
options.how: A small lane after o2's move refuses docs/decisions/ and docs/debts/ cites, keeps the Drops-lines exception, and reads both paths from the one layout file.
options.label: Refuse the new layout paths too
options.lose: One extra refusal; it changes a guard, so it gets review rounds.

options.gain: Every cite can be opened directly.
options.label: Retire the rule and allow path cites
options.lose: Each move breaks them. A deletion breaks an id cite too, so this only helps for the 71 moved files.

ref: o2 (one layout for every repo), PR #607
title: Should the guard refuse docs/decisions/... path cites after the folder move?
why: Most broken cites came from deletions, which no rule saves. A move is the one case where ids win, and o2 is that move. The exception keeps the one path use with a real reader.
